_about: Scientific data library, domain medicine: the universal columns of the game's body/data/medicine.json tables, written by scripts/split_data.py. Same columns/rows schema as the game's tables. `id` is stable (see README); `source` holds source keys from sources.json ('; ' separated) or 'open'. Mark is the review state of these columns. A null in a column the engine's data/*.json holds by the same id means the engine file is the home of that value.

diseases.title: The disease list (period names in brackets)
diseases.source: Causes and courses are modern medicine (textbook; MED-* keys in SOURCES.md). Period presence and names from Trapham 1679, Sloane 1707, Woodall 1617, Moyle 1693, the Burnard mortality study, the Hektoen ship-fever article and the Cardiff sea-surgeons piece. Mortality figures are ranges, untreated, confidence as given per row.

wounds.title: Wound kinds, what each does, and how long it heals
wounds.source: Healing phases: hemostasis at once, inflammation 1 to 4 days, proliferation 4 to 21 days, remodelling 21 days to a year (MED-HEAL). Period handling from Woodall and Moyle. Infection and mortality ranges are the keeper's reading of the sources, medium confidence.

pain.title: Pain (0 to 10) and shock
pain.source: The 0 to 10 numeric rating scale is standard clinical practice; the mapping to game effects is the keeper's model. Period analgesia: laudanum (Sydenham's tincture of opium, 1660s), rum, biting a bullet.

treatments.title: What a surgeon of 1650 to 1730 could do (and whether it worked)
treatments.source: Woodall, The Surgeon's Mate (1617); Moyle, Chirurgus Marinus (1693); the humoral tradition (bleeding, purging, emetics, sweating); Sydenham (laudanum, bark); Pare's ligature (1564); Petit's tourniquet (1718); inoculation 1721. MED-WOOD, MED-MOYLE, MED-HUM, MED-LIND
treatments.note: No cited source gives a hygiene exposure multiplier (unswabbed days, lice, foul water, wet-season port) or a death risk with treatment; both stay unset (hygiene defaults to 1 in the engine). See flags/medicine.md.

healing.title: Healing clock modifiers
healing.source: Wound healing needs protein, vitamin C (collagen) and zinc; scurvy reopens old wounds (Lind, and modern collagen biology); age slows healing; infection resets the clock; rest speeds it. MED-HEAL
rows: Collagen integrity at or below the first daily loss from intact tissue in anatomy.tissues.connective-tissue-collagen (1 minus that row's daily integrity decrement); otherwise x1

immunity.title: Immunity and resistance
immunity.source: Lifelong immunity after yellow fever and smallpox; partial after falciparum malaria; none after dysentery or influenza strains; Constitution as the hidden resistance stat is Rex's (STATS.md).
rows: partial, fades after a year away
none: they return when the nutrient does not
The seasoning (a state, not a disease)

a newcomer who has survived his first bouts of the local fevers is 'seasoned': an immunity record, held here, not a row in the disease list. Period estimates put newcomer deaths in Jamaica's first years as high as a third (Burnard; confidence low on the fraction)

exposure.title: Conditions from the air (named here, caused by ATMOSPHERE, GAS_DYNAMICS and the body)
exposure.source: Standard emergency medicine for hypoxia, hypercapnia, carbon monoxide poisoning, smoke inhalation, irritant injury, hydrogen sulphide and altitude illness; the period could do nothing but carry the man into the air and bleed him. Each condition is a pattern of the body's states, never a timer (the brief's rule, kept).
